question.problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)={e}^{-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}}?$

choices.value: A family of spheres centered at the origin
A family of spheres centered at $(0,0,{e}^{-1})$
A family of spheres centered at $(0,0,e)$
A family of surfaces given by ${z}^{2}+c={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ for $c\ne 0$
A family of surfaces given by  ${z}^{2}+c={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ for $c>0$

current_example.problem: Find the family of surfaces that describe the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y, z) = \ln(x^2 + 2y^2 - z^2).$
current_example.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}) & =c \\ {x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-{z}^{2} & ={e}^{c} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{e}^{c}}+\frac{2{y}^{2}}{{e}^{c}}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{{e}^{c}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get a family of hyperboloids of one sheet:

$$
\dfrac{x^2}{e^c} + \dfrac{y^2}{e^c/2} - \dfrac{z^2}{e^c} =  1, \qquad c \in (-\infty,\infty)
$$
